newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng Index soars to close above 13,000.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index soars to close above 13,000.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks rose steeply for the second day in a row on Thursday, closing above the 13,000-point level for the first time since mid-March as gains on Wall Street propelled prices higher, brokers said.
The blue-chip Hang Seng Index soared 117.48 points, or 0.91 percent, to finish at 13,020.78. Turnover was HK$12.50 billion compared with HK$13.82 billion on Wednesday.

Brokers said the market was boosted by continued buying in blue chips, especially property stocks, following recent gains on Wall Street and a declining U.S. long bond yield amid easing fears of higher interest rates.
The last time the Hang Seng closed above 13,000 points was on March 12 when it ended at 13,119.13. Since then it has been plagued by concerns about property prices and interest rates.

"Foreign investors started to turn to properties on expectations that the sector is going to recover in the second half of the year as interest rate worries ease," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
The U.S. 30-year long bond yield has fallen below seven percent, which Kwong said indicated rate pressures were easing.
He said this fuelled hopes of a recovery in the local property market.
Cheung Kong rose HK$1.50 to HK$69.50 and Sun Hung Kai Properties added HK$2.50 to HK$86.50.
Sino Land jumped HK$0.65 to HK$8.00 after Morgan Stanley Capital Index said it would include the stock in its indices. Varitronix, which rose HK$1.25 at HK$12.05, is also to be included.
But HSBC Holdings eased HK$1.00 to HK$195.00.
Analysts said trading was likely to be cautious on Friday ahead of U.S. April employment data.
Tony Yung, research director at Tai Fook Securities Co Ltd, said negative data might prompt a correction.
Selective buying on H-shares lifted the Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index up 6.93 points, or 0.65 percent, to close at 1,074.38.
Toy maker Kin Yat 0638.HK closed its first trading day at HK$1.64 after opening at HK$2.20.
The company offered 85 million shares at HK$1.28 each in an initial public offering in Hong Kong.
Hang Seng Index May futures advanced 150 points to 12,970 and the June contract gained 150 points to 13,000.
